scope: 6.2 Train-aug only. No Challenge Set family is listed or reserved.

count/present.construction: "<N> <att> lesions are present in the liver." then a separate "The largest, in <seg>, measures <size>." (N as digits or a word).
examples: Seven hypoattenuating lesions are present in the liver. The largest, in segment 6, measures 6.3 x 3.3 cm.
3 hypoattenuating lesions are present in the liver. The largest, in segments 3/5, measures 8.3 x 5.0 cm.

count/in_total.construction: "... lesions, <N> in total; the largest lies in <seg> with a size of <size>."
examples: The liver shows hypoattenuating lesions, 6 in total; the largest lies in segment 1 with a size of 4.1 x 3.6 cm.
The liver shows hypoattenuating lesions, 4 in total; the largest lies in segment 5 with a size of 5.1 x 4.4 cm.

count/listed.construction: Labelled list "Lesion 1: <seg>, <size>, <att>. Lesion 2: ..." (2-5 lesions, shuffled; count = number of labels).
examples: Lesion 1: segment 3, 0.9 x 0.7 cm, hyperattenuating. Lesion 2: segment 6, 2.9 x 2.5 cm, hypoattenuating. Lesion 3: segments 2/8, 6.1 x 5.4 cm, hypoattenuating. Lesion 4: segment 6, 4.5 x 3.6 cm, hypoattenuating. Lesion 5: segment 4, 2.5 x 2.1 cm, hyperattenuating.
Lesion 1: segment 2, 2.5 x 2.1 cm, hypoattenuating. Lesion 2: segment 4, 1.6 x 1.2 cm, hypoattenuating.

count/another.construction: "One <att> lesion is present in <seg> (<size>). Another lesion ... A further lesion ... Yet another lesion ..." (2-4 lesions; count = number of sentences).
examples: One hypoattenuating lesion is present in segment 6 (4.0 x 3.0 cm). Another lesion is present in segment 1 (2.0 x 1.0 cm). A further lesion is present in segment 4 (1.5 x 0.9 cm).
One hyperattenuating lesion is present in segments 2/7 (4.4 x 3.8 cm). Another lesion is present in segment 5 (1.2 x 0.6 cm).

count/only_one.construction: "Only one <att> lesion is present ..." or "There is a lone <att> lesion ...".
examples: There is a lone hypoattenuating lesion in segment 7 of 7.7 x 6.3 cm.
There is a lone hyperattenuating lesion in segment 1 of 8.7 x 4.6 cm.

count/vague.construction: "Innumerable / A few / Scattered / Various <att> lesions are present throughout the liver; the largest, in <seg>, has a size of <size>." Count is unstated.
examples: Various hyperattenuating lesions are present throughout the liver; the largest, in segments 4/8, has a size of 3.3 x 2.9 cm.
A few isoattenuating lesions are present throughout the liver; the largest, in segment 2, has a size of 5.8 x 3.7 cm.

size/single_mm.construction: One dimension in millimetres: "A <att> lesion of <NN> mm lies in <seg>."
examples: A hypoattenuating lesion of 48 mm lies in segment 5.
An isoattenuating lesion of 80 mm lies in segments 2/6.
An isoattenuating lesion of 2.9 cm by 2.0 cm is present in segment 7.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 2.6 cm by 1.5 cm is present in segments 3/4.

size/greatest_diameter.construction: "... has a greatest diameter of <a> cm."
examples: A hypoattenuating lesion located at segment 4 has a greatest diameter of 3.2 cm.
A hypoattenuating lesion located at segment 8 has a greatest diameter of 6.7 cm.

size/three_in_size.construction: Three dimensions with the unit after each: "<a> cm x <b> cm x <c> cm in size".
examples: There is a hyperattenuating lesion at segment 2, 6.6 cm x 4.7 cm x 2.0 cm in size.
There is a hypoattenuating lesion at segment 2, 4.9 cm x 4.4 cm x 1.9 cm in size.

size/reaching.construction: "..., reaching <a> cm, ..." or "as large as <a> cm".
examples: A hyperattenuating lesion at segments 1/8, reaching 8.3 cm, is present.
A hyperattenuating lesion at segment 2, reaching 3.7 cm, is present.

segment/roman.construction: Roman numerals: "in liver segment VI", "(segment VI)".
examples: A hyperattenuating lesion of 4.2 x 3.8 cm is present in liver segment II.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 7.7 x 6.8 cm is present (segment I).
A hypoattenuating lesion of 3.6 x 2.0 cm is present in subsegment IVa.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 4.0 x 2.9 cm is present in subsegment IVa.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 4.0 x 2.2 cm is present in segment 2 according to Couinaud.
An isoattenuating lesion of 3.0 x 1.7 cm is present in segment 4 according to Couinaud.

segment/ordinal.construction: "in the 5th segment of the liver", "within segment five", "in the fifth segment of the liver".
examples: A hyperattenuating lesion of 2.3 x 2.0 cm is present within segment eight.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 8.0 x 4.0 cm is present in the 1st segment of the liver.

segment/range.construction: "extending from segment <n> into segment <n+1>", "spanning segments <n> to <n+1>".
examples: A hyperattenuating lesion of 7.3 x 4.0 cm is present extending from segment 3 into segment 4.
A hyperattenuating lesion of 3.0 x 2.6 cm is present extending from segment 6 into segment 7.

segment/lobe.construction: Lobe only: "in the right/left liver lobe", "within the right/left lobe". Segments are unstated.
examples: A hypoattenuating lesion of 8.4 x 5.2 cm is present within the left lobe.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 9.0 x 6.8 cm is present in the right liver lobe.

attenuation/appearing.construction: "hypodense / hyperdense / isodense": "A lesion appearing hypodense ...", "<Seg> contains a hypodense focus of <size>."
examples: A lesion appearing isodense is present in segments 1/5, with a size of 4.1 x 3.1 cm.
Segments 4/5 contains a hyperdense focus of 4.9 x 2.7 cm.
A lesion of equal density is present in segment 6, with a size of 3.4 x 2.3 cm.
A lesion of high density is present in segments 1/7, with a size of 2.1 x 1.4 cm.

attenuation/relative.construction: Comparison with the liver: "darker/brighter than the adjacent hepatic tissue", "less dense than / denser than background liver", "as dense as ...", "indistinguishable in density from background liver".
examples: In segment 3 there is a 5.0 x 3.6 cm lesion, less dense than background liver.
In segment 5 there is a 3.8 x 2.5 cm lesion, brighter than the adjacent hepatic tissue.

attenuation/separate.construction: In its own sentence after the lesion: "It appears hypoattenuating.", "Its attenuation is low/high.", "Its attenuation matches the liver."
examples: There is a lesion in segments 3/6 with a size of 5.3 x 4.5 cm. It appears hyperattenuating.
There is a lesion in segment 4 with a size of 2.7 x 2.1 cm. Its attenuation is low.

order/size_list.construction: One sentence listing "<seg> (<size>)" for 2-4 lesions, ascending or shuffled: "<Att> lesions are seen in segment 1 (...) and segments 3/6 (...)."
examples: Hypoattenuating lesions are seen in segment 1 (1.3 x 1.1 cm) and segments 3/6 (2.3 x 1.6 cm).
Hypoattenuating lesions are seen in segment 4 (1.9 x 1.0 cm), segment 3 (3.3 x 2.0 cm), and segment 7 (1.1 x 0.8 cm).

order/larger_of_two.construction: Smaller lesion first, then "The larger of the two, <att>, lies in <seg> with a size of <size>."
examples: An isoattenuating lesion of 3.3 x 2.6 cm lies in segment 8. The larger of the two, hyperattenuating, lies in segment 4 with a size of 5.8 x 3.7 cm.
A hypoattenuating lesion of 4.7 x 2.6 cm lies in segment 4. The larger of the two, isoattenuating, lies in segment 5 with a size of 5.9 x 3.2 cm.

order/there_is.construction: "There are lesions in <seg>, a <size> <att> lesion; in <seg>, a <size> <att> lesion; ..." (2-4, shuffled).
examples: There are lesions in segments 2/4, a 7.1 x 3.7 cm hypoattenuating lesion; in segment 1, a 2.4 x 2.0 cm hyperattenuating lesion; in segment 2, a 5.3 x 3.0 cm hyperattenuating lesion.
There are lesions in segment 5, a 0.4 x 0.3 cm hyperattenuating lesion; in segment 5, a 1.6 x 0.9 cm hypoattenuating lesion.

paraphrase/single.construction: Other nouns and verbs for one lesion: "<Seg> is the site of a <size> <att> focus / tumor / space-occupying lesion.", "A <att> <noun> sits in <seg>; size <size>."
examples: A hyperattenuating space-occupying lesion sits in segments 2/7; size 8.2 x 6.8 cm.
A hypoattenuating focus sits in segment 2; size 7.2 x 5.9 cm.

paraphrase/multiple.construction: "The liver holds <N> <att> foci/tumors. The most prominent / greatest / principal of these sits in <seg>, sized <size>; the others are under <x> cm."
examples: The liver holds two hyperattenuating foci. The most prominent of these sits in segment 6, sized 7.6 x 6.1 cm; the others are under 7.2 cm.
The liver holds four isoattenuating tumors. The greatest of these sits in segments 2/8, sized 5.7 x 3.4 cm; the others are under 5.3 cm.

repeat/single.construction: One lesion, restated in a tail: "There is a <att> lesion of <size> at <seg>. IMPRESSION: <att> lesion, <seg>, <size>." (count stays 1).
examples: There is a hyperattenuating lesion of 8.3 x 5.2 cm at segment 2. IMPRESSION: hyperattenuating lesion, segment 2, 8.3 x 5.2 cm.
There is a hypoattenuating lesion of 8.9 x 4.5 cm at segment 5. IMPRESSION: hypoattenuating lesion, segment 5, 8.9 x 4.5 cm.

repeat/multiple.construction: Listed lesions, then "IMPRESSION: <N> lesions, of which the largest is <size>, <seg>."
examples: Hypoattenuating lesions are seen in segments 3/6 (3.2 x 2.3 cm) and segment 1 (2.0 x 1.6 cm). IMPRESSION: 2 lesions, of which the largest is 3.2 x 2.3 cm, segments 3/6.

Hyperattenuating lesions are seen in segments 5/6 (2.5 x 1.7 cm), segment 1 (2.0 x 1.0 cm), segment 7 (1.2 x 1.0 cm), and segment 5 (0.4 x 0.3 cm). IMPRESSION: 4 lesions, of which the largest is 2.5 x 1.7 cm, segments 5/6.

non_lesion/length.construction: A liver length beside one lesion: "Liver length is <x> cm." (not a lesion size).
examples: Liver length is 17.3 cm. Segment 8 contains a hyperattenuating lesion of 3.7 x 2.9 cm.
Liver length is 18.5 cm. Segment 6 contains a hypoattenuating lesion of 3.0 x 1.5 cm.

non_lesion/duct.construction: "The common hepatic duct measures <x> cm." beside one lesion.
examples: Segment 7 contains a hypoattenuating lesion of 3.4 x 2.2 cm. The common hepatic duct measures 0.9 cm.
Segments 3/7 contains a hyperattenuating lesion of 6.7 x 5.4 cm. The common hepatic duct measures 0.9 cm.

non_lesion/node.construction: "Near the liver, a lymph node of <x> cm is noted." beside one lesion.
examples: Near the liver, a lymph node of 13.7 cm is noted. Segment 3 contains an isoattenuating lesion of 8.8 x 7.4 cm.
Near the liver, a lymph node of 6.1 cm is noted. Segments 4/8 contains a hyperattenuating lesion of 3.6 x 2.8 cm.

real.description: Real Train reports (liver-only text), unchanged; targets come from the source labels.

ocr.description: Character noise (swapped, dropped or replaced letters, digit/letter confusions) applied to real Train reports and to generated items of the families above (`ocr` subtype = the family it was applied to).
